answer: Challenge-Derived Key Ladder. Each new agent identity must solve a fresh challenge derived from the current garden state hash, and its first action must forge a signed transcript binding that solution to a randomly assigned beacon slot. The transcript is unrepeatable: replaying it fails because the slot rotates per epoch. An attacker pays one full compute-plus-latency cycle per identity, so mass registration scales linearly in real time and hardware, not in cheap copies.
